title: Executing Bearish Supply
hook: The bearish sequence, walked from the 4H story to the 5M retest, one decision at a time.

launchpad.outcome: Execute a bearish supply setup step by step: read the HTF story, confirm the 15M break, follow the 5M sequence, mark the zone, wait for BOS #3 and the retest.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What has to be true before a bearish retest becomes an entry?

takeaways: The HTF story sets the direction. For a supply trade it has to be bearish.
BOS #1 and BOS #2 are not entries. They are steps in the sequence.
Correction #2’s last bullish candle forms the supply zone. BOS #3 activates it.
After BOS #3, wait for the retest. If price never comes back, don’t chase.

slides.headline: Now the mirror image: bearish supply.
slides.line: You’ll walk a full bearish setup, from the higher-timeframe story to the 5M retest, and make the call at every step.

slides.headline: Start with the story, not the 5M.
slides.line: Tap each card. This is the HTF (higher timeframe) context for this setup.

cards.label: 4H context
cards.sub: Bearish. Price is in the upper half of the 4H range and correcting.

cards.label: 1H structure
cards.sub: Bearish 1H structure. Price is reacting from a 1H lower high.

cards.label: HTF ICC
cards.sub: HTF ICC: bearish Indication, Correction in progress.

check.prompt: Which direction does this context support?

options.label: Bearish. Look for a supply setup.
options.why: Right. The 4H, the 1H and the HTF ICC are all bearish, so you look for a bearish sequence and a supply zone.

options.label: Bullish. Look for a demand setup.
options.feedback: Read the cards again. The 4H, the 1H and the HTF ICC are all bearish. Higher-timeframe ICC supplies the direction.

slides.headline: Wait for the 15M to break with the story.
slides.line: Press the button. Watch for a 15M candle to close below the 15M level.

steps.caption: BOS #1 (break of structure). A 15M candle closes below the 15M level, in the direction of the HTF story.

check.prompt: BOS #1 just closed. What’s your next move?

options.label: Sell now, the break is confirmed
options.feedback: Don’t enter simply because BOS #1 occurred. It’s the first of three breaks, and there’s no zone yet.

options.label: Switch to the 5M and wait for Correction #1
options.why: Yes. BOS #1 starts the sequence. The 5M still has to build two corrections, the zone and two more breaks.

slides.headline: Find the 5M close that continues the move.
slides.line: Correction #1 is marked in peach. Now find BOS #2.
slides.ask: Tap the first 5M candle that closes below the low Correction #1 pulled back from.
slides.why: That’s BOS #2: the first 5M close below the low Correction #1 pulled back from. A wick alone wouldn’t count.

after.caption: BOS #2. The move continued. It’s still not an entry. Now you wait for Correction #2.

slides.headline: Correction #2 creates the supply zone.
slides.line: Correction #2 has just ended. Find the one candle that forms the zone, not the whole correction.
slides.ask: Tap the last bullish candle of Correction #2.
slides.why: That’s the last bullish candle of Correction #2. It forms the supply zone.

after.caption: The zone uses this candle’s full high-to-low range. It’s only a potential zone until BOS #3 happens.

slides.headline: Wait for BOS #3 to activate the zone.
slides.line: Press the button. Sellers need a 5M close below the low Correction #2 pulled back from.

steps.caption: BOS #3. A 5M candle closes below the low Correction #2 pulled back from. The zone is now active.

check.prompt: BOS #3 just closed and price is moving down fast. What do you do?

options.label: Wait for price to return to the zone
options.why: Right. After BOS #3, you wait for the retest. If price never comes back, you don’t chase it.

options.label: Sell now, before it runs away
options.feedback: That’s chasing. BOS #3 activates the zone, but the entry model only applies when price returns to it.

slides.headline: Spot the moment price comes back.
slides.line: The zone is active. Watch for the first return to it.
slides.ask: Tap the first candle that trades back up into the supply zone.
slides.why: That’s the retest: the first time price returns to the active zone after BOS #3.

after.caption: The working model places a limit at the zone’s low, its near edge. A bearish candle closing out of the zone is the additional-confirmation option.

slides.headline: Every bearish trade passes every step.
slides.line: Tap each step. If one is missing, there is no trade.

steps.label: The HTF story is bearish
steps.sub: The 4H context, the 1H structure and the HTF ICC point down.

steps.label: BOS #1 on the 15M
steps.sub: A 15M candle closes below the 15M level.

steps.label: Correction #1, then BOS #2
steps.sub: A 5M pullback, then a 5M close below the low it pulled back from.

steps.label: Correction #2 creates the zone
steps.sub: Its last bullish candle forms the supply zone.

steps.label: BOS #3, then the retest
steps.sub: A 5M close activates the zone. Then price has to come back to it.

slides.quote: Supply is demand in the mirror. The sequence never changes.

slides.prompt: In your own words, walk through a bearish supply trade from the 4H to the entry.
slides.modelAnswer: First the HTF story has to be bearish. Then a 15M candle closes below the 15M level for BOS #1. On the 5M, Correction #1 pulls back and BOS #2 closes below the low it pulled back from. Correction #2 follows, and its last bullish candle forms the supply zone. BOS #3 activates the zone, and then I wait for price to return to it. If price never comes back, I don’t chase it.
